skill.name: flutter-animations
skill.description: Comprehensive guide for implementing Flutter animations, including implicit widgets, AnimationController patterns, hero transitions, staggered motion, physics simulations, performance guidance, and reusable examples.
skill.summary: Build smooth Flutter motion with practical animation patterns and references.
skill.author: madteacher

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives. The sensitive detections are Flutter super.key syntax, the blocker detections are Dart lifecycle or documentation text, and the external command detections are Markdown backticks around Dart examples. No prompt injection, credential exposure, command execution, or exfiltration intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Use static Tweens when possible (avoid recreating)
- Avoid complex widget trees inside hero
- Too slow? Increase stiffness or decrease mass
- Ensure physics animations don't cause motion sickness
const DebugStaggeredWidget({super.key, required this.controller, required this.animations});
// Calculate stagger based on grid position
- Use appropriate curves for natural motion (see `Curves` class)
- Use `timeDilation` to slow animations during debugging
- Wrap images in `Material` with transparent color for "pop" effect
- Consider `HeroMode` to disable hero animations when needed
- Use `Interval` to offset animations in time
- Use `setState()` in animation listeners when `AnimatedBuilder` suffices
- Avoid nested implicit animations for performance
- Consider performance (avoid heavy widgets in animation builds)

content.value_statement: Flutter motion can be hard to choose and implement correctly. This skill guides animation selection, code patterns, performance, and accessibility.
actual_capabilities: Selects implicit, explicit, hero, staggered, or physics animation approaches.
Explains AnimationController, Tween, CurvedAnimation, AnimatedWidget, and AnimatedBuilder patterns.
Provides reusable Flutter examples for common animation workflows.
Guides hero transitions, radial hero effects, and shared element motion.
Covers performance, lifecycle disposal, curves, debugging, and accessibility concerns.
limitations: Does not run or test Flutter projects automatically.
Examples may need adaptation for project architecture and Flutter version.
Does not replace product design review for motion timing and accessibility.
Does not create visual assets or animation files.

use_cases.title: Add Simple State Motion
use_cases.description: Use implicit animation widgets to animate size, color, opacity, padding, or alignment changes.
use_cases.target_user: Flutter developers adding small interface refinements

use_cases.title: Build Controlled Animations
use_cases.description: Use AnimationController patterns for coordinated, reversible, or status-aware motion.

use_cases.title: Design Screen Transitions
use_cases.description: Plan hero, staggered, and physics-based motion for polished app navigation and reveals.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Animation Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a new Flutter animation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the best Flutter animation type for this UI change: [describe the widget and trigger].

prompt_templates.title: Implement an Implicit Animation
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer adding a simple state-driven transition.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Flutter implicit animation plan for [property] when [state] changes. Include widget choice and timing guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor to AnimationController
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer needs lifecycle control and multiple animated properties.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this animation idea into an explicit AnimationController design: [describe motion, duration, curves, and states].

prompt_templates.title: Design Complex Motion
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for coordinated app transitions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production Flutter motion system with hero transitions, staggered reveals, physics behavior, performance checks, and accessibility fallbacks.

output_examples.input: I need a card to expand smoothly when selected.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use AnimatedContainer with a short duration, an ease curve, and state-driven width, height, and color changes.

output_examples.input: I need a logo to grow, fade in, then reverse when complete.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use AnimationController with Tween values, a status listener, and AnimatedBuilder to limit rebuild work.

output_examples.input: I need a photo grid item to open into a detail screen.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use matching Hero tags, similar widget trees on both screens, and a Material wrapper for route transition polish.

best_practices: Start with implicit animations for simple state changes.
Dispose AnimationController instances in widget disposal.
Respect reduced motion preferences and avoid excessive motion.
anti_patterns: Do not use setState in every animation tick when AnimatedBuilder is enough.
Do not create nested animation trees without measuring performance.
Do not use hero animations with inconsistent tags or unrelated widget trees.

faq.question: Which Flutter animation type should I use first?
faq.answer: Use implicit animations for simple property changes. Use explicit animations when you need lifecycle or timing control.

faq.question: Does this skill include code examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Flutter patterns and template files for implicit, explicit, hero, and staggered animations.

faq.question: Can it help with AnimationController lifecycle?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains controller setup, vsync usage, status listeners, and disposal.

faq.question: Does it cover hero animations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers basic shared element transitions, radial hero effects, tags, and route transition considerations.

faq.question: Can it improve animation performance?
faq.answer: It provides performance guidance, including AnimatedBuilder usage, controller disposal, and avoiding heavy animated builds.

faq.question: Does it run Flutter tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance, but users must run and validate animations in their Flutter project.
